newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada monthly GDP rises 0.2 percent in August.
newsitem.headline: Canada monthly GDP rises 0.2 percent in August.

text.p: Canada's real gross domestic product, seasonally adjusted, rose 0.2 percent in August after a 0.5 percent rise in July, Statistics Canada said Thursday.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast real GDP to rise 0.2 percent in August.
Note: GDP figures are in billions of dollars, seasonally adjusted at annual rates at factor cost, constant 1986 dollars.
Statistics Canada said continuing increases in the mining sector, construction and wholesale trade, as well as renewed strength in transportation and storage services, fueled the August increase.
Agriculture and community, business and personal services also posted small increases, but manufacturing production fell after surging in July.
Activity in retail trade and financial services also slowed in August.

Statistics Canada said GDP in the first two months of the third quarter rose 0.6 percent, higher on average than the second quarter. The two-month increase compared with advances of 0.5 percent in the first and 0.4 percent in the second quarter.
